newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jets will defend themselves, Perry warns Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jets will defend themselves, Perry warns Iraq.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Perry warned Iraq on Monday that U.S. jets will not tolerate threats from Iraqi anti-aircraft batteries and will continue to fire missiles if pilots get indications they are being targeted by ground radar.

"(Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein has very clear warning already from the fact that we conduct 100 sorties (flights) a day over this area" of southern Iraq, Perry told reporters. "We conduct them with airplanes that are very well armed and quite capable of taking care of themselves."

Perry responded to questions hours after the second reported incident in three days in which a U.S. F-16 fighter fired a missile at an Iraqi mobile missile battery when the pilots received electronic indications they were being targeted from the ground.

The Pentagon said on Sunday that the first incident, which occurred on Saturday, was a mistake because an investigation later indicated radar had not tracked the F-16. Iraq on Monday denied that either incident had even occurred.

"We will continue those missions," over the no-fly zone, said Perry. "They (pilots) will continue with the rules of engagement that they now have. And those rules of engagement are that if their warning equipment on the airplane indicates that they are being tracked they are authorised to launch anti-radiation missiles at the site."

He said it was not known yet whether the U.S. missiles had struck the Iraqi batteries and that both incidents were under investigation. But Perry also added that the zone had been very quiet for at least a week prior to the shooting with no indication that Iraq was increasing activity against U.S. and allied warplanes.
